# OrbitOCR

> OrbitOCR is a free, open-source Circle to Search-style utility for Windows 10/11: press Ctrl+Shift+S to freeze and dim the whole desktop, then copy text off the screen or freehand-circle an image to search it with Google Lens. OCR runs 100% on-device.

## Key facts

- Product name: OrbitOCR
- Category: Windows desktop utility (screen OCR + visual search)
- Platform: Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, and Windows 11 — x64
- License: MIT
- Price: free, no paid tier
- Current version: 1.0.0
- Install: portable single .exe from GitHub Releases; no installer, no admin rights, no .NET runtime required
- Download: https://github.com/torpidno/OrbitOCR/releases/latest/download/OrbitOCR.exe
- Source code: https://github.com/torpidno/OrbitOCR
- Website: https://torpidno.github.io/OrbitOCR/

## What it does

- Global hotkey (default Ctrl+Shift+S) freezes and dims the entire multi-monitor desktop.
- Detected words become interactive: click one or drag across a phrase to select it.
- Text mode actions: Copy Text, Search Google.
- Image mode actions: Search with Lens, Copy Image, Save Image (PNG/JPEG), plus Copy Text when text is detected inside the region.
- Freehand lasso with a glowing trail and draggable corner handles to refine a region.
- Configurable global hotkey, system-tray resident, ~30 MB idle footprint, PerMonitorV2 DPI aware.
- Optional auto-copy on selection, sound feedback, and start with Windows (launches minimized to the tray).

## Privacy

- OCR runs locally using the OCR engine already built into Windows (Windows.Media.Ocr).
- No cloud OCR, no telemetry, no accounts, no crash reporting, no auto-updater phoning home.
- The only actions that send anything off-device are Search Google and Search with Lens, triggered explicitly by the user, and they simply open the default browser.

## How it compares

- vs PowerToys Text Extractor: PowerToys extracts text from a region; OrbitOCR freezes the whole multi-monitor desktop first, supports direct click/drag text selection, and adds freehand circle to Google Lens.
- vs Snipping Tool: built-in and requires capturing a screenshot; OrbitOCR works from one hotkey with no capture step and adds Google Lens image search.
- vs ShareX: ShareX is a full screenshot suite that requires installation; OrbitOCR is a single portable .exe focused on one flow.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, or Windows 11, x64.
- At least one Windows OCR language pack (English ships with Windows).
- No .NET runtime installation required.

## FAQ

Q: Is there a Circle to Search for Windows?
A: Windows has no native equivalent. OrbitOCR is a free, open-source alternative that brings the same freeze-and-select workflow to Windows 10 and 11.

Q: Is OrbitOCR free?
A: Yes. It is MIT-licensed with no paid tier.

Q: Does OrbitOCR work offline?
A: Yes. OCR runs locally via the Windows OCR engine; no internet connection is needed to recognize text.

Q: Does OrbitOCR send my data anywhere?
A: Only if you explicitly click Search Google or Search with Lens, which open your browser. Nothing else leaves the device, and there is no telemetry.
